sourceQuestions.sourceText: Draw a line to match each word to its meaning. Reduce Reuse Recycle / use the same thing again, break it down and make something new, use less, buy fewer things
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Reduce – use less, buy fewer things • Reuse – use the same thing again • Recycle – break it down and make something new

sourceQuestions.sourceText: A sentence under a picture that tells us about it is called a ___.
Where do we find the blurb?
What do we use a contents page for?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: To find where things are in the book / which page to go to.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write reduce, reuse or recycle. a Filling your water bottle again and again. b Putting cans in the recycling bin. c Buying fewer plastic bags.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a reuse • b recycle • c reduce

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Why is a plastic bag dangerous for a turtle?
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: It can eat it because it looks like food, or get tangled in it.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: True or false? Write T or F. a An information book tells true facts. b A label is usually a long story.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a T • b F — a label is one or two words.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: On the back of this page, draw something you could make from a reused plastic bottle. Give it a label and write a caption under it.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: A drawing of something made from a bottle (pencil pot, plant pot, bird feeder…), a short label (one or two words with a line) and a caption sentence underneath.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: An information book tells us ( made-up stories ) ( true facts ) ( rhymes )
A caption is ( a sentence about a picture ) ( the price of the book ) ( the back cover )
Putting a can in the recycling bin is ( reducing ) ( reusing ) ( recycling )
The blurb is on the ( back cover ) ( contents page ) ( first page of the story )
A label is usually ( a whole page ) ( one or two words ) ( a long story )
